description: Signal connections in a scene file. Each connection answers with its flags as the number and as flagNames; persist is on every connection, since a scene saves no other kind. A connection carries binds, the values passed after the signal's own, and unbinds, how many of the signal's own are dropped first, as the editor's connect dialog offers them; each is answered only when there is one. A connect of a pair already connected says alreadyConnected, with flagsBefore, bindsBefore and unbindsBefore when it changed them, and keeps the binds and unbinds it had unless the call gives new ones. A connect to a method the target does not have is still written, as the editor's own dialog allows, since the method may be written next; methodFound false says so, and until the method exists the signal fails each time it is emitted. That holds only without binds and unbinds: the engine makes a connection that binds or unbinds arguments only to a method its target has, and a scene loads without one aimed elsewhere, so such a connect is refused. A file can hold one already, written by hand or before its method was renamed: the engine loads the scene without it and a save drops it, so every tool that writes a .tscn puts it back as the file held it and says so under unmadeConnections, a write to a binary .scn holding one is refused, and a disconnect takes it out. One whose method cannot take what the signal passes, with its binds and unbinds (too few or too many arguments, an object where the method takes a value or the reverse, or an engine class unrelated to the one it takes), is written too, and answers argumentsFit false with misfit saying why; list gives each connection its methodFound, and misfit when it has one. list marks editable false on a connection a scene this one instances or inherits makes, on its own root as well as inside it, and names that scene under madeIn; only that scene can change it, so a disconnect of one is refused. Through the editor when one serves the project; with none, a headless engine runs the editor's own tool and the answer says so under writtenBy, or readBy for a read. That engine runs every script of the file, where the editor runs only tool scripts, so what a script changes as the file loads or as a property is set is put back before anything is saved, and a file where that cannot be done, such as a scene whose script does not compile, is refused and nothing is written. Each file the written one refers to is named by its uid, as the editor names it, except a file the project's uid cache has no uid for yet (one made since the project was last scanned), which is named by path and listed under namedByPath with the call that scans it. An editor of the project that is running and has not reached this server is waited for rather than written around. A scene is saved as the engine holds it once the file has loaded, and one property can set others as it loads, as anchors_preset gives a centred Control both its grow directions, so a scene not last saved by an editor can gain, change or lose lines the call did not ask for, on any node the file held, the one it names among them: alsoSaved lists each as {node, property, was, saved}, was left out where the file set nothing and saved where it now sets nothing. What a set itself moved on its node is under alsoChanged rather than here, and neither a node the call adds nor the format lines (header uid, load_steps, unique_id) are listed. The scene loads as it did; only its text changed. Operations: connect (needs sourceNodePath, signalName, targetNodePath, methodName): connect a signal to a method; disconnect (needs sourceNodePath, signalName, targetNodePath, methodName): remove a connection; list: every connection in the scene.

binds.description: connect: the values passed to the method after the signal's own, written as a read answers them. [] takes them off. Default: those the connection already has. Only for op connect.

flags.description: connect: Object.ConnectFlags added together: deferred 1, persist 2, one_shot 4, reference_counted 8, append_source_object 16. Persist is added either way. A read can also name inherited, 32, on a connection an instanced scene makes, which is not given. Only for op connect.

methodName.description: The method on that node, called when it emits. Only for ops connect, disconnect.

nodePath.description: list: only connections involving this node. Only for op list.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

signalName.description: The signal it emits, such as "pressed". Only for ops connect, disconnect.

sourceNodePath.description: The node that emits. Only for ops connect, disconnect.

targetNodePath.description: The node whose method is called. Only for ops connect, disconnect.

unbinds.description: connect: how many of the signal's own arguments are dropped, from the end, before the binds are added. 0 takes it off. Default: what the connection already has. Only for op connect.

title: Scene signals
